_note: Shriram Finance (consolidated; subsidiaries are immaterial since the Dec-2024 sale of Shriram Housing Finance) lender model, as of 30-Sep-2026 on a Q1FY27 basis. Sources: Q1FY27 results and investor update (24-Jul-2026) and call (24-Jul-2026, transcript filed 27-Jul-2026); Q4FY26 results and investor update (24-Apr-2026) and call; annual reports FY2021-22 (STFC), FY2023-24, FY2024-25, FY2025-26; Screener.in for the statements (FY25 P&L patched to the audited continuing-operations basis, see tools/authoring/SHRIRAMFIN.patch.js). The MUFG preferential issue (47.11 cr shares at ₹840.93 = ₹39,617.98 cr, allotted 8-Apr-2026) is IN the base case as FY27 capital.

history._why: aum = standalone AUM incl. direct-assignment (off-book) loans at March (FY18-FY22 Shriram Transport Finance before the merger; FY23 onward the merged Shriram Finance). provisions = impairment on financial instruments and feeIncome = revenue from operations less interest income, both consolidated, on the basis Screener uses for that year (FY23-FY24 include Shriram Housing Finance, consolidated then; FY25 continuing operations). FY23 ratios are distorted by the merger (FY23 income includes Shriram City Union for the whole year while Mar-22 AUM is STFC alone); FY23-FY24 income includes SHFL (FY24 turnover ₹1,430 cr, total assets ₹11,859 cr) which standalone AUM excludes, so FY24 yield and NIM read high (SHFL turnover was ~0.7% of average AUM).

src.FY26: Q4FY26 audited consolidated results p29 (24-Apr-2026); AUM: Q4FY26 investor update p8
src.FY25: FY25 annual report, consolidated P&L p387 (continuing operations); AUM: FY26 annual report p34
src.FY23-FY24: FY24 annual report consolidated P&L p343; AUM: FY26 annual report p34 (five-year chart)
src.FY21-FY22: STFC FY22 annual report consolidated P&L p237
src.FY18-FY22 AUM: STFC FY22 annual report p5 (five-year chart, on-book + off-book)

_aumGrowthWhy: FY27 guidance ~18% (budget set in Apr-2026, reiterated 24-Jul-2026, to be reassessed after Q2 on the monsoon); Q1FY27 +15.3% YoY / +3.8% QoQ, Q2 guided at 15-16%. FY26 grew 14.85% against a 15% guide. The MUFG capital lets the company target 18-20% (FY26 annual report). We take 17% in FY27 (as PL and Emkay do) and 18% after, when the new-vehicle, gold and MSME pushes have scale.
_yieldOnAumWhy: Interest income ÷ average AUM: 16.50% FY26; 16.8% annualised in Q1FY27, helped by interest on ~₹38,500 cr of cash and investments parked from the MUFG money. As that liquidity goes into loans and the mix shifts to new vehicles (16-17% of disbursements, targeted at 20-25%) where management is passing on its lower funding cost, we take the yield down ~15-20bp a year.
_feeIncomePctWhy: Fees, commission, fair-value gains and other operating income ÷ average AUM: 0.52% FY26, 0.63% in Q1FY27 (incl. ₹185 cr of gains on liquid funds holding unused MUFG money). Back to ~0.55% as the liquidity is used.
_costOfFundsWhy: Interest expense ÷ average of opening and closing borrowings: 8.88% FY26 (company 'cost of liabilities' 8.59% at Mar-26, 8.56% at Jun-26; incremental 7.77% after the Apr-2026 AAA upgrades; bank money ~8%). The underlying FY27E rate is ~8.55%, but the MUFG money cut borrowings in April (₹2,50,690 cr in Mar-26 to ₹2,32,639 cr in Jun-26), so true average FY27 borrowings are ~₹9,000 cr below the engine's opening/closing average; we enter 8.25% so that interest expense matches Q1 actual plus Q2-Q4 at 8.55% on a rising balance (₹20,800 cr). FY28E 8.40% and FY29E 8.25% (≈8.15% / 8.0% on the company basis): new money at 7.8-8.0% replaces older, dearer debt; no rate cuts assumed (repo 5.25%, CPI forecast raised to 5.1%).
_opexPctWhy: Operating expenses incl. fee and commission expenses and depreciation ÷ average AUM: 2.82% FY26 (2.85% FY25), 2.76% annualised in Q1FY27. ~150 new branches and manpower in FY27 and wage inflation (Q1 staff cost +17%); management expects cost ratios broadly stable as volumes absorb the cost. Small scale gains after FY27. Cost-to-income falls to ~26% because income rises with the extra equity, not because costs fall.
_creditCostWhy: Impairment ÷ average AUM: 2.22% FY24 (incl. SHFL), 2.18% FY25, 1.89% FY26, 1.90% annualised in Q1FY27. Management guides 'around 2%' on its own basis (credit cost to total assets: 1.65% FY26, 1.66% Q1FY27), so on that yardstick FY26 came in well below guidance. We keep 1.95-2.0% of average AUM (≈1.7% of total assets): the current run-rate plus a margin for a deficient monsoon (IMD forecast 90% of normal, El Nino) and faster growth in MSME and personal loans.
_payoutWhy: FY26 dividend ₹10.80 a share (₹4.80 interim + ₹6.00 final) = 20.3% of EPS; FY24-FY25 payout 19-23% (FY25 incl. a special from the SHFL sale). The FY26 final dividend was paid on the enlarged share count incl. MUFG's shares (₹1,411.7 cr).
_minorityPctWhy: No minority interests since Shriram Housing Finance was sold (Dec-2024); subsidiaries left (Shriram Overseas Investments) are wholly owned.
_otherIncomeWhy: Screener 'other income' outside operations: ₹52 cr FY26 (₹58 cr before small exceptional items), ₹18 cr in Q1FY27; plus ~₹27 cr pre-tax equivalent of the ~₹20 cr share of profit of the associate Shriram Automall (SFL share FY26 ₹20.5 cr, Q1FY27 ₹5.5 cr), which the engine cannot carry separately.
_capitalRaiseWhy: MUFG Bank preferential issue: 47,11,21,055 shares at ₹840.93 = ₹39,617.98 cr, allotted 8-Apr-2026 (primary capital; MUFG 20.0% on a fully diluted basis), plus ₹0.89 cr of ESOP exercises in Q1FY27. No further raise is planned: management says the capital supports growth for 4-5 years (Motilal Oswal, 29-Sep-2026) and the FY26 annual report targets a calibrated rise in leverage to ~4.5x over 5-6 years.
_newSharesWhy: Shares rise from 188.14 cr (FY26 Profit for EPS ÷ EPS; 188.16 cr reported at Mar-26) to 235.29 cr at Jun-26 (Q1FY27 investor update p30): 47.11 cr to MUFG plus 0.02 cr ESOP. EPS uses year-end shares; the allotment on 8-Apr-2026 makes that close to the weighted count.

valuation._why: Ke = 6.5% + 1.15 × 6% = 13.4% (house rf and ERP; beta 1.15: a cyclical lender to small truck operators and MSMEs, above Bajaj Finance's 1.1, tempered by AAA funding and low leverage after the MUFG money). sustainableRoe 16% = the 15-17% the franchise earned in FY24-FY26 (company basis, pre-MUFG) once leverage climbs back toward the company's ~4.5x target over 5-6 years; ROE is only 12.8-13.5% in FY27-FY28 because of the extra equity. g = 10% long-run book growth in the justified P/B. Residual income fades ROE to 16% over 8 years, payout rising to 30%, 6% terminal growth.

methods.name: P/B
methods.why: The street's method (Motilal Oswal 2.2x FY28E book, ICICI Direct ~2.1x FY28E, Emkay 2.1x FY28E, PL 2.4x Mar-28 adjusted book). 1.5x = own median one-year-forward P/B since Apr-2021 (1.4x, book adjusted for the MUFG issue before it was announced) × the listed-lender move vs five-year medians (−6.6%, Shriram excluded) × the post-merger regime since Apr-2023 (1.6x ÷ 1.4x). Bull 2.0x = close to the Feb-2026 peak (2.1x) and the street; bear 1.2x = where it traded in FY22 before the merger.

methods.name: Justified P/B
methods.why: (ROE − g) ÷ (Ke − g) = (16 − 10) ÷ (13.4 − 10) on book at the 12-month target date.

methods.name: Residual income
methods.why: Book plus the present value of profit above the 13.4% cost of equity, ROE fading to 16%, rolled forward 6 months.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check only. 9x = median forward P/E since Apr-2021 (9.2x, FY25 EPS taken before the ₹1,489 cr SHFL gain) × listed-lender P/E move vs five-year medians (−17.4%) × post-merger regime (10.8x ÷ 9.2x). Bull = post-merger median 10.8x; bear = 25th percentile since 2021 (7.6x, adjusted).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: MUFG-backed growth: AUM +19/20/20% (top of the 18-20% ambition), yield +10bp, opex 5bp lower, credit cost ~1.7% of AUM (FY26-type), long-run ROE 18% as leverage rebuilds faster; the market keeps paying close to its Feb-2026 peak.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: A weak monsoon and costlier money: AUM +12/13/13%, yield −30bp (pass-through and competition in new vehicles), funding 30bp dearer (rates rise with inflation), credit cost ~2.6% of AUM (FY25 level plus rural stress); long-run ROE 13%; the multiple falls back to its pre-merger level.
